title: RC Aircraft
summary: A fully club-built fixed-wing RC aircraft, from airfoil selection to first flight.
description: Our flagship aeronautics project: a fixed-wing radio-controlled aircraft designed and built entirely by members. The team handles the complete cycle — airfoil selection, CAD modelling, structural sizing, laser-cut ribs, motor and battery sizing, then ground and flight testing. The project doubles as a training platform for new members joining the department.

title: Drone Lab
summary: Quadcopter platform for autonomous flight experiments and aerial imaging.
description: A modular quadcopter platform used to explore flight controllers, PID tuning and autonomous missions. The long-term goal is an aerial-imaging drone capable of automated mapping flights over campus.

title: Model Rocket Program
summary: Solid-motor model rockets with onboard altimetry and recovery systems.
description: The Aerospace Department's stepping stone to bigger launches: a series of model rockets with parachute recovery and onboard flight computers logging altitude and acceleration. Each iteration flies higher and carries more instrumentation.

title: CubeSat Concept Study
summary: A 1U CubeSat feasibility study focused on Earth observation for Morocco.
description: A student-led feasibility study for a 1U CubeSat mission: mission definition, subsystem budgets (power, link, mass), and an Earth-observation payload concept relevant to Morocco. The study prepares the club for national and international CanSat/CubeSat competitions.

title: Flight Simulation Corner
summary: A fixed simulator setup where members learn real flight procedures.
description: A permanent flight-simulation setup with yoke, throttle quadrant and rudder pedals. Used for initiation sessions during integration week and for regular 'virtual airline' evenings where members fly real procedures on real routes.

title: Technical Workshop Series
summary: Recurring hands-on workshops: CAD, aerodynamics, electronics, astronomy.
description: A recurring series of hands-on workshops open to all students: CAD for aerospace, introduction to aerodynamics, soldering and embedded electronics, and telescope operation ahead of astronomy nights.
